key_insight: MDQEC-QAS learns a single meta-decoder that can adapt syndrome-to-recovery decisions across multiple quantum error-correction codes and noise settings, with confidence-gated fallback improving robustness when direct prediction is uncertain.
engineering_relevance: The work points to hardware-aware decoder design for practical quantum error correction, where circuit constraints, code diversity, and safe selective recovery matter as much as raw prediction accuracy.
method: Meta-learn syndrome-to-recovery mapping across FiveQubit, Steane, Planar3x3, and Planar5x5 codes.
Use hardware-aware quantum architecture search to choose VQC qubit count, depth, and entangling topology.
Apply confidence-gated recovery to defer uncertain cases to a safer fallback decoder.
evidence_signal: Across five evaluation regimes, Meta-MLP and hardware-aware VQC reached teacher-label accuracies of 0.9993/0.9400, 0.9118/0.8495, 0.9342/0.8415, 0.6304/0.5678, and 0.7548/0.7143, while confidence gating cut interpolation logical-failure ratios from 12.08 and 25.91 to 1.71 and 1.11.
watch_item: High teacher-label accuracy does not guarantee low logical failure, especially in the hardest Planar5x5 setting, so deployment needs confidence calibration and fallback integration.
paper_title: MDQEC-QAS: Meta-Decoding for Quantum Error Correction with Hardware-Aware VQC Search and Confidence-Gated Recovery
